title: Lissity descends along surjective etale pullback
statement: Let $p:T\to Y$ be etale and surjective [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $F$ be a set-valued sheaf on the small etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. If $p^{-1}F$ is lisse (locally constant with finite geometric stalks), then $F$ is lisse. Inverse image is the constructed set-sheaf inverse-image functor of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves].

source.place: ## Proof, finite-algebra calculation and final paragraph

proof.text: Composition with p is left adjoint to base change on small etale categories. Pass this adjunction to continuous sheaf pushforwards. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies constructed set inverse image with etale localization restriction. Identify restriction to an etale object with localization restriction through Etale.overSheafEquiv. This equivalence transports constant sheaves; the comparison is constructed as the preimage of the natural presheaf isomorphism.

Take a cover of T trivializing p inverse image F and compose its arrows with p. Every point of Y lifts to T and then to that cover, so the composite family is a surjective etale cover. On each member map the restriction comparison through its localizationRestriction functor. Over.mapComp identifies the two composed restrictions with restriction along the composite map. Transport the constant sheaf through these isomorphisms. This supplies a trivializing cover for F.

For a geometric point s of Y, surjectivity supplies a point t of T over s default. Mathlib exists_fac_of_etale_of_isSepClosed lifts s to a geometric point a of T because the field is algebraically closed. Use the proved set inverse-image stalk comparison to obtain a bijection from the finite stalk of p inverse image F at a to the stalk of F at a followed by p. Finite.of_surjective and the equality a followed by p equals s give the required finite stalk.
